title: LPT: bounded agentic LLM loops for de novo protein binder design
summary: LPT orchestrates fixed stages of LLM agents with a curated database of about 14,000 papers to design protein binders from one natural-language prompt. An LLM with database access answered 41 of 48 test questions correctly, versus none without access. Three end-to-end campaigns targeted CALCRL/RAMP1, PD-1/PD-L1 and PVR-TIGIT, with a high in silico success rate across several folding models. The results are computational; the abstract reports no experimental binding data.
ai_technology: LPT framework: fixed orchestration of bounded LLM agentic loops with literature database and design tools
organization: Hubrecht Institute for Developmental Biology and Stem Cell Research

evidence.tested: The database-backed LLM answered 41 of 48 questions drawn from database key findings. Designed binders were cross-validated with multiple folding models.
evidence.unknown: The abstract reports only in silico results and states no wet-lab validation.
evidence.ai_role: LLM stages identified the design intent, selected targets, structures and hotspot residues, and designed candidate binders.
